items.text: Subscribers per 1,000 views read 0.6 on the latest read, carried from an older finished episode, against a usual 2.8. In E8, DesignerTom gained 9.2 per 1,000 views against 3.6 for Dive Club.
items.recommendation: Test one spoken subscribe ask at a mid-show high point, pinned in chat on both channels. Then see whether Dive Club's gain per 1,000 views moves toward DesignerTom's.

items.text: Announce posts got played at 24.2 against a usual 30.6. E5's launch ran soft at 1,127 YouTube views against a typical 1,751. X carries 36.9 share of all watching.
items.recommendation: Test two announce posts for the next episode: one the day before with the watch link in the first line, and one at go-live. Post both on X and on YouTube, then compare plays.

items.text: Subscribers brought 37,490 YouTube views, 71.6 share of the total. End screens brought 16 views and Shorts brought 6. Search brought only 4.7 share.
items.recommendation: Add an end screen to every episode that points to the next-newest one, and build a playlist of the best guest episodes. Then check whether end-screen and playlist views rise.

items.text: Early exits repeat. In E9, 5.1 of every 100 viewers left about an eighth of the way in. In E5, 5.3 left at the same point, during chatty stretches before the main segment.
items.recommendation: Trim the banter before the first real segment next episode and start the guest or demo inside ten minutes. Then check whether fewer viewers leave that early.

items.text: E9 drew 109 average live viewers, kept each one 14.2 minutes, and had 73 people chatting. The show's usual average live turnout is 62.
items.recommendation: Test another episode built around audience-submitted segments like E9's. Ask chat in advance to send entries, then compare average live viewers and chatters with E9.
